sourceToRenderedComparison: The left and right open horizontal leads terminate outside the same connected junctions 1 and 2. The lower branch joins those junctions without crossings or extra nodes.
A remains inside the upper circular meter between point 1 and R. The upper wire meets both opposite sides, with no line through the meter interior.
R remains an unfilled rectangular resistor to the right of A and left of point 2. Both upper wires meet the side midpoints; R is below the rectangle.
V remains inside a lower circular meter. Its center is below and to the right of the A center. Lower wires meet both opposite horizontal sides, with no interior conducting line.
The voltmeter branch spans points 1 and 2, including A and R in the upper section. It does not move to the two resistor-only contacts.
There is exactly one rightward current arrow above R, with I above the arrow. The arrow is visibly separate from conducting wires and agrees with the prose's point-1-to-point-2 current.

All six source labels are retained as 1, 2, A, R, V and I. No E arrow, voltage arrow, potential label, polarity sign, voltage equation, numerical value, extra instrument, cultural wording or answer annotation is added.
Small connection dots, exact circles, straight lines, right-angle corners, a regular rectangle, semantic colors and clean type are explicitly recorded as modern regularization, not new source givens.

Circuit topology and all six labels match the other two widths. Both meters, resistor rectangle and single I arrow are clear; no clipping, label collision, missing conductor or extra arrow.
